findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() can crash recovery code login page for user-storage credentials
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` can now return an empty `Optional` when the user has recovery codes only in a user storage provider that implements `isConfiguredFor`/`isValid` but does not implement `getCredentials` (making `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` empty). The previous local-only lookup also used `.get()`, but this PR newly supports federated-only recovery codes, so this path is newly reachable. The unchecked `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException`, causing a 500 instead of rendering the recovery-code login form.

findings.title: User-storage recovery codes are not consumed, so codes remain reusable and reconfigure is never required
findings.body: After a valid recovery code is submitted, this code relies on `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` to decide whether to remove the credential and add the `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` required action. For a credential stored in user storage, `isValid` is dispatched to the user storage provider. The test provider (and any provider that implements `CredentialInputValidator` without mutating stored credentials) only compares the submitted raw code against the stored list and does not remove the used code. The model returned by `getCredential` therefore continues to report that codes remain, so `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true, used codes stay valid indefinitely, and the required action is never added. Recovery codes must be consumed either by the framework or by an enforced provider contract; otherwise the one-time property is lost for federated storage.
